writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 169 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
It is widely accepted that an important goal of education is to help students learn how to learn. In my view, teaching learners to acquire knowledge on their own matters far more than simply filling their heads with facts, because the ability to learn lasts a lifetime.
The reason is that knowledge itself keeps changing, while the skill of learning does not. Consider two students: one memorizes every formula the teacher offers, and the other masters how to find, question and apply new information. When they leave campus and face problems no textbook has covered, the first often feels lost, whereas the second keeps growing. My own experience confirms this. In college I taught myself programming through online courses; what my teachers really gave me was not the code, but the confidence and method to explore an unfamiliar field by myself.
For these reasons, education should do more than deliver content. Once students truly learn how to learn, they hold a key that opens every door throughout their lives.

cloze.title: 2023年6月·第3套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: You might not know yourself as well as you think. According to a new study, people are __(26)__ accurate judges of only some of their behaviors. While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits, this new study __(27)__ how well people understand how they are acting from one moment to the next. Researchers asked participants to wear audio recorders that automatically __(28)__ every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m. to record 30 seconds of audio. These participants were then emailed surveys four times a day asking them to __(29)__ how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day. The study used data from 248 participants, all of whom answered questions about their behavior for two __(30)__ weeks and wore the audio device for one of those weeks.
passages.zh: 你可能并不像自己以为的那样了解自己。根据一项新的研究，人们只有在判断自己的某些行为时才比较准确。以往关于人们对自身了解程度的大多数研究，都集中于长期的人格特征，而这项新研究探究的是，人们对自己从一个时刻到下一个时刻的行为方式究竟了解多少。研究人员要求参与者佩戴录音设备，该设备会在早上7点至次日凌晨2点之间每隔9.5分钟自动启动，录下30秒的音频。随后，研究人员每天四次向这些参与者发送调查问卷，请他们回忆自己在一天中特定的某个小时里表现得有多外向、随和或尽责。这项研究采用了248名参与者的数据，他们都连续两周回答有关自己行为的问题，并在其中一周佩戴了录音设备。

passages.en: Six laboratory assistants rated each participant's audio clips to see how their observations compared with people's __(31)__ of themselves. The six assistants were generally in agreement with one another about how the people they were observing acted. Further, participants' ratings of their own behaviors agreed with observers' for how outgoing and how conscientious they were being. But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness. Some of this __(32)__ could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read __(33)__ like body language, but there are __(34)__ other explanations, as people should be able to hear when a participant is being kind versus being rude. The weak agreement between how participants thought they were acting and what observers heard could be because people would rather __(35)__ rude behavior.
passages.zh: 六名实验室助理对每位参与者的音频片段进行评分，以了解他们的观察结果与参与者对自己的评价有多大程度的可比性。这六名助理对于所观察对象的行为方式通常意见一致。此外，参与者对自身行为的评价与观察者的评价相一致，具体表现在他们对自己的外向程度和尽责程度的判断上。但在随和程度方面，参与者与外部观察者之间的一致性要小得多。这种差异部分可能是因为观察者只能听到音频片段，因而无法解读肢体语言之类的线索；但可能还有其他解释，因为参与者表现得友善还是粗鲁，人们应该能够从声音中听出来。参与者认为自己的行为方式与观察者听到的情况之间之所以一致性较低，可能是因为人们往往不愿承认自己有粗鲁的行为。

rows.text: L) relatively副词
空在 are 与 accurate judges 之间，修饰形容词 accurate
与 of only some of their behaviors 的"有限/不完全"语义共振 句尾 only some of their behaviors 已经把人对自己行为的判断范围限定为"只有部分"，作者要表达的是"对自身行为只能算是相对准确的判断者"，relatively 这种程度副词正好与"only some"形成呼应——不是绝对准确、只是相对准确。
H)probably情态偏"可能性"，与后文"only some"的限定语义错位 probably 表"很可能"，强调命题的真假概率；但原句要表达的不是"人可能是准确判断者"，而是"在准确程度上是相对的、有限的"。况且 probably 留给第 34 题更贴——那里 are __ other explanations 需要的正是"很可能还有其他解释"，这个词更值得留给后面。
I) probes动词
主语 this new study 后缺谓语

研究"深入探究"问题是惯用搭配 句意是"这项新研究深入探究人们对自己片刻行为的理解程度"，与前句 While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits 的对比正好——以前的研究做长期人格、这项新研究则"深入考察"短时行为。a study probes/explores how... 是学术语境的高频表达。
B)articulatesarticulate 偏"清晰表达观点"，主语应是人或文章 articulates 的典型主语是人/作者/政策文件，意为"清晰阐明（一种立场）"；用在"研究"上多见于"该研究阐明了某结论"，但本句宾语是 how-从句问号式的"研究问题"，与"探究/调查"的语义更贴，与 articulate 的"明确表达已有观点"语义错位。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— B articulates 三单形态完全合，靠语义才能区分。articulates 在 this new study ___ how... 的位置看似也通，但 articulate 指"清晰表达观点"，主语应是已经形成立场的人或文件；而本句宾语是 how-从句的研究问题，本质是"研究在调查/探究某问题"。一句话防坑：研究＋how 问题＝probe/explore，研究＋that 结论＝articulate/state。
A) activated动词
that 引导定语从句，空作从句谓语

录音机"被启动/启动"是描述设备机制的标准表达 录音机"每 9.5 分钟自动启动一次以录 30 秒音频"才符合实验设计。activated 在此为过去式作谓语，与全文研究描述的过去时态一致（如 asked、used、were 都是过去时），且 automatically activated 是描述自动设备的常见搭配 audio recorders that automatically __(28)__ every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m.。

I)probes时态为现在时、且语义不指设备启动 probes 是第三人称单数现在时，与复数主语 recorders 不一致；语义上指"探究/调查"，多与人或问题搭配，不与"录音机每 9.5 分钟探究"搭配。 B)articulates单复数不匹配 + 语义指"清晰表达" articulates 主语应是人（清晰表达），与"录音机"在主谓搭配上严重失配，单复数也与复数 recorders 不一致。 K)recall语义指人的"回忆"，与设备主语冲突 recall 的主语通常是人，意为"回忆/想起"；机器"recall every 9.5 minutes"不成立，且 K 在 29 题有更刚需的位置（让参与者"回忆"自己当时的行为）。 O)terminate语义反向："终止"与"启动录音"完全相反 若代入 terminate every 9.5 minutes，意为"每 9.5 分钟终止一次"，与后半句 to record 30 seconds of audio（启动后录 30 秒）形成逻辑矛盾。
K) recall动词
asking them to＋空，不定式中的动词原形

回忆某时段自己有多外向/友善＝实验任务 原句要求参与者评估"自己在某一小时里有多外向、友善或尽责" how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day，这是典型的"回忆性自评"任务，recall 表"回想起"与"a particular hour of the day（白天某一小时）"的过去时间状语精准匹配。
F)deny语义反向："否认"自己有多外向不成立 ask them to deny how outgoing they were 意为"让他们否认自己当时有多外向"，逻辑荒谬；且 F 在 35 题处有更贴切的位置（参与者"否认"粗鲁行为）。 O)terminate搭配错误：终止"自己有多外向"不通 terminate 通常与活动、合同、过程搭配，不能与 how-从句搭配描述自我评估。
D) consecutive形容词
数词 two 与名词 weeks 之间的限定位置
two consecutive weeks＝"连续两周"是高频固定搭配 原文说参与者要回答两周的行为问卷、其中一周还要戴录音设备，强调的是"连着进行的两周"。consecutive 与 weeks 是英语里"连续 N 周"的标准说法，语义与研究设计完全吻合 answered questions about their behavior for two __(30)__ weeks。

J)random与"两周"严密的实验时段矛盾 random weeks 意为"随机的（任选的）几周"，但研究是两周连续追踪、并明确其中一周戴录音设备 wore the audio device for one of those weeks，时间是确定段落而非随机选取，与 random 的"任意性"冲突。 M)saturated搭配不成立、语义不通 saturated 多用于"饱和脂肪/被…浸透/市场饱和"，从未与"weeks"构成日常表达；语义上也无法解释一段"被饱和的两周"，搭配直接证伪。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— J random 词性、搭配都看似通。random 是形容词、可修饰 weeks、读起来也顺，但与原文研究设计"连续两周＋其中一周戴录音"的精密时段冲突。一句话防坑：先去原文找时间安排的描述（wore the audio device for one of those weeks），看时段是"连续"还是"随机"再下笔。
C) assessment名词
形容词性物主代词 people's 后接名词

与前文 observations 形成"他评 vs 自评"对比 句子在比较"助理们的 observations"与"参与者对自己的 ___"，这正是研究的核心对照——他人观察 vs 自我评估。assessment 意为"评估/判断"，与 observations 在抽象层级上对等，构成"observations of A vs assessment of A"的标准学术对照 how their observations compared with people's __(31)__ of themselves。
G)discrepancydiscrepancy 是"差异"本身、不是"参与者对自己的判断" discrepancy of themselves 不成立——人不会"对自己有差异"。况且 G 在 32 题处恰好用来描述"自评与他评之间的分歧"，那里才是它的归宿。
G) discrepancy名词
代词 this 后＋空 → 抽象名词作主语

回指上文"自评与他评在 agreeableness 上分歧明显" 上句说 But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness. 这正是"分歧/不一致"。this ___ 概括的就是这种 agreeableness 上的不一致，discrepancy 恰是"差异/出入"的标准名词，与 agreement 反义构成上下文呼应。
E) cues名词
动词 read 的宾语 + like body language 的同位列举
cues 与 body language 同属"非语言线索"语义集 cues 指"线索/信号"，nonverbal cues / visual cues 与 body language 构成同位列举，语义自然贴合："观察者无法读取诸如肢体语言这类的线索" could not read __(33)__ like body language——正好解释为什么仅听音频会让宜人评分出现偏差。
N)symptomssymptoms 是"病症"，与"肢体语言"不同类 symptoms 多指疾病征候，无法与 body language 构成同位列举；read symptoms 在医学语境可成立，但与本文心理学行为观察主题不符。
H) probably副词
are 与 other explanations 之间的存在句结构

but 后引出"可能还有别的解释"的推测语气 前句 could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read __(33)__ like body language 给出一种解释（可能因为只听音频），但作者用 but 引出另一种猜测：很可能还有别的解释。probably 恰好承担"作者的推测口吻"，与 could be 的不确定基调一致。
F) deny动词
would rather＋空 → 动词原形

人们"宁可否认"自己粗鲁——解释自评偏差 上文说参与者对"宜人/友善"的自评与外部观察分歧大 the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness，作者在此给出心理学解释：人们宁愿"否认"自己当时表现得粗鲁，所以自评偏向"我没那么粗"。deny rude behavior 是"否认粗鲁行为"的标准搭配，正好解释了自我评估和观察之间的落差。
O)terminatewould rather terminate 与心理回避语义不符 terminate rude behavior 字面是"终止粗鲁行为"，但上下文重点不是"停止粗鲁"——录音已结束、行为已发生——而是"自评时是否承认"。terminate 也不解释为何观察者听到了"粗鲁"而当事人自评却没有，逻辑不对路。

longreading.title: 2023年6月·第3套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) We're experiencing the rebirth of smallness. Farmers markets, tiny homes, and brew pubs all exemplify our love of smallness. So do charter schools, coffee shops, and local bookstores. Small is often (but not always) more affordable, healthier, and sustainable, but its finest characteristic, the one that turns charm into love, is that going small allows us to be more fully who we are.
passages.zh: 我们正在经历小规模事物的复兴。农贸市场、微型住宅和精酿酒吧都体现了我们对小规模事物的喜爱。特许学校、咖啡馆和本地书店也是如此。小规模通常（但并非总是）更经济、更健康、更具可持续性，但它最突出的特点，也是将魅力转化为喜爱的原因，在于选择小规模能让我们更充分地成为真正的自己。

passages.en: B) In higher education the trend is mostly in the opposite direction: Universities with 20,000 or 30,000 students are considered "mid-sized". The nation's largest university, Arizona State University, has 80,000 students on campus and aims to enroll another 100,000 students online. At the other end of the spectrum is a handful of colleges that have fewer than a hundred students on campus and no online courses: colleges such as Sterling College, Thomas More College of Liberal Arts, and Deep Springs College. These colleges are so small that they can only be called "tiny."
passages.zh: 在高等教育领域，趋势大多正好相反：拥有两万或三万名学生的大学被认为是“中等规模”的。全国最大的大学亚利桑那州立大学在校学生有八万人，并计划再招收十万名在线学生。处于另一端的是少数几所校园内学生不足一百人且不开设在线课程的学院，例如斯特林学院、托马斯·莫尔文理学院和深泉学院。这些学院规模小到只能称为“微型学院”。

passages.en: C) Tiny colleges focus not just on a young person's intellect, but on the young person as a whole. Equally important, tiny colleges ask, "How can education contribute to human flourishing and the well-being of the world?" And they shape a college experience to address that question. They replace concerns about institutional growth with attention to the growth of students as fully developed participants in their communities.
passages.zh: 微型学院关注的不仅是年轻人的智力，也关注年轻人作为一个完整的人的整体发展。同样重要的是，微型学院会提出这样的问题：“教育如何促进人的蓬勃发展以及世界的福祉？”它们也会围绕这一问题来塑造大学经历。它们不再关注机构的发展壮大，而是关注学生的成长，使他们成为所在社区中得到充分发展的参与者。

passages.en: D) I've had the privilege of teaching at three different institutions of higher learning during my career—a small liberal arts college and two mid-sized public universities. I've also been profoundly disappointed in each of these institutions, and in many of my colleagues, especially when it comes to helping students and preparing them for the many responsibilities of adulthood. Administrators focus on the business of running a university, and most faculty focus on their scholarship and teaching their discipline. Little deliberate attention is given to how students mature as individuals and social beings.
passages.zh: 在我的职业生涯中，我有幸在三所不同的高等教育机构任教——一所小型文理学院和两所中等规模的公立大学。然而，我也对这三所机构以及我的许多同事深感失望，尤其是在帮助学生、为他们承担成年后的诸多责任做好准备方面。管理人员专注于经营大学的事务，大多数教师则专注于自己的学术研究和本学科的教学。人们很少有意识地关注学生如何成长为成熟的个体和社会成员。

passages.en: E) Having just retired from teaching at a public university, I'm now returning to my hometown of Flagstaff, Arizona, to establish a tiny college—Flagstaff College. I'm convinced there's a need for another type of education, one devoted to helping students come into their own and into this beautiful and troubled world. Young people need an education that will provide them with meaning, hope, courage, and passion, as well as information and skills. Large institutions, I believe, are particularly ill-suited to this type of education.
passages.zh: 刚刚从一所公立大学的教学岗位上退休，我现在正回到家乡亚利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫，创办一所微型学院——弗拉格斯塔夫学院。我确信，我们需要另一种教育，一种致力于帮助学生充分发展自我、走进这个美丽而又充满困扰的世界的教育。年轻人需要的教育，不仅要为他们提供信息和技能，还要赋予他们意义、希望、勇气和热情。在我看来，大型机构尤其不适合开展这种教育。

passages.en: F) There's no "best of" list when it comes to tiny colleges, at least not yet. But around the country people are creating new colleges that provide an alternative to small liberal arts colleges, large public universities, and online education.
passages.zh: 说到微型学院，至少目前还没有什么“最佳院校”榜单。但在全国各地，人们正在创建新的学院，为小型文理学院、大型公立大学和在线教育提供一种替代选择。

passages.en: G) With only 26 students, Deep Springs is the smallest college in the country and, quite likely, the most atypical(非典型的). Located on a working cattle ranch on the California-Nevada border, Deep Springs is a private, residential, two-year college for men, committed to educating students for "a life of service to humanity." Founded by the electricity tycoon(大亨) L.L. Nunn in 1917, Deep Springs "curriculum" revolves around academics, labor, and self-governance. In addition to their courses, students are charged with running the 155-acre ranch and overseeing the functioning of the college. Students chair both the admissions and the curriculum committees.
passages.zh: 深泉学院只有26名学生，是全国规模最小、很可能也是最非典型的学院。它坐落在加利福尼亚州与内华达州交界处的一座正在经营的牧牛场上，是一所私立寄宿制两年制男子学院，致力于培养学生“为人类服务的一生”。深泉学院由电力大亨L.L. Nunn于1917年创办，其“课程”围绕学业、劳动和自我管理展开。除了学习课程之外，学生还负责经营这座155英亩的牧场，并监督学院的运转。招生委员会和课程委员会均由学生担任主席。

passages.en: H) "Living in close community with one's teachers and fellow students, and being forced to take on adult responsibilities, makes for one's growth as a person," says William Hunt, who graduated last year. "To exist for very long in a community like that, you have to get over the question of whether you're sufficiently talented or principled and get started worrying about how you can stretch yourself and your peers, how much you can manage to learn with them."
passages.zh: “与教师和同学在紧密的共同体中生活，并被迫承担成年人的责任，会促使一个人成长为更成熟的人，”去年毕业的威廉·亨特说。“要在这样的共同体中长期生活下去，你必须不再纠结于自己是否足够有才能或有原则，而是开始思考如何拓展自己和同伴的能力，以及你们能够共同学到多少东西。”

passages.en: I) Sterling College, in Craftsbury Common, Vermont, is also very small—fewer than 100 students. Unlike Deep Springs, Sterling focuses its curriculum on environmental and social justice issues, but like Deep Springs it places a high value on personal responsibility and manual labor. According to its catalog, a college education at Sterling combines "rigorous academics, roll-up-your-sleeves challenges, and good old hard work."
passages.zh: 位于佛蒙特州克拉夫茨伯里康芒的斯特林学院同样规模很小，学生人数不足100人。与深泉学院不同，斯特林学院的课程重点是环境问题和社会正义问题；但和深泉学院一样，它高度重视个人责任和体力劳动。根据该校的课程目录，斯特林学院的大学教育融合了“严谨的学术学习、需要卷起袖子迎接的挑战，以及扎扎实实的辛勤劳动”。

passages.en: J) The average tuition at a small liberal-arts college is $30,000 to $40,000 a year, not including the cost of living on campus, as compared to $8,000 to $10,000 a year for tuition alone at a public university. Of the tiny colleges, only Deep Springs doesn't charge tuition or room and board; students pay only for books and the cost of traveling to and from college. If tiny schools are to become a player on the higher education scene, they will need to find a way to be truly affordable.
passages.zh: 小型文理学院的平均学费为每年3万至4万美元，不包括在校生活费用；相比之下，公立大学仅学费一项每年为8000至1万美元。在这些微型学院中，只有深泉学院不收取学费、住宿费和伙食费；学生只需支付书费以及往返学院的交通费用。如果微型学校要在高等教育领域占有一席之地，就需要找到真正让教育变得负担得起的方法。

passages.en: K) Doing so may not be that difficult so long as they do not pattern themselves too closely on existing norms. We've come to believe that a good college should have many academic programs and excellent facilities, posh(豪华的) dorms, an array of athletic programs, and a world-class student activity center. Imagine a good college without a climbing wall! We also have accepted the idea that college presidents, and their many vice-presidents, should be paid like their counterparts in the business world and that higher education requires an elaborate, up-to-date technology infrastructure. All of this drives up the cost of education.
passages.zh: 只要不完全照搬现有的规范，这件事也许并不难做到。我们已经逐渐相信，一所好的大学应该拥有众多学术项目和优良设施、豪华宿舍、各种体育项目以及世界一流的学生活动中心。试想一下，一所没有攀岩墙的好大学！我们也接受了这样的观念：大学校长及其众多副校长应当像商界同行那样获得高薪，而高等教育需要一套复杂且与时俱进的技术基础设施。所有这些都会推高教育成本。

passages.en: L) The "trick" to making tiny colleges affordable, if that's the right word, is simplicity. At its core, education is a human-to-human interaction. Reflecting on his own college education, President Garfield once commented that an ideal college would consist of nothing more than the legendary teacher Mark Hopkins on one end of a log and a student on the other. The economics of a tiny college, in other words, might be similar to that of a tiny house. Because it is small, a tiny house costs less to build and less to furnish, insure, and maintain. But the economic benefits of a small house don't end there. Tiny homes discourage homeowners from buying stuff that they really don't need, because there's no place to put it.
passages.zh: 让微型学院变得负担得起的“诀窍”，如果这个词用得恰当的话，就是简单。在本质上，教育是人与人之间的互动。加菲尔德校长曾反思自己的大学教育，并评论说，理想的大学应该不过是传奇教师马克·霍普金斯坐在一根木头的一端，学生坐在另一端。换句话说，微型学院的经济模式或许类似于微型住宅。由于面积小，微型住宅建造成本更低，配置家具、投保和维护的费用也更少。但小住宅带来的经济效益并不止于此。微型住宅会抑制房主购买那些确实不需要的东西，因为没有地方存放它们。

passages.en: M) I'm a late convert to the idea of tiny colleges, and I fully understand the need for many diverse types of educational institutions. Academic research and job training are important, but tiny colleges aren't suited for either. The educational needs of a complex society are themselves complex, and no single model can meet all of these needs. But I'm now convinced there's an educational need that's now going almost completely unmet: namely, the need to help young people transition into adulthood. Tiny colleges can do this better than any other type of educational institution.
passages.zh: 我后来才转而认同微型学院这一理念，而且我完全理解社会需要许多不同类型的教育机构。学术研究和职业培训都很重要，但微型学院并不适合承担这两项任务。复杂社会的教育需求本身就是复杂的，没有任何单一模式能够满足所有这些需求。但我现在确信，有一种教育需求几乎完全没有得到满足：也就是帮助年轻人过渡到成年。微型学院能够比其他任何类型的教育机构更好地做到这一点。

passages.en: N) The ultimate justification for a tiny college is the conviction that each of us comes into our full humanity by close interaction with those who know and care for us, and that one of the basic purposes of higher education is social. Although we give lip service to the idea that a college education will make us better people, when all's said and done, we think of higher education primarily in economic terms. We've come to think of higher education as a means to make a living rather than make a life. We've also come to see higher education as a private good rather than a public one. Tiny colleges are not the answer to all of our educational requirements, but they're an answer to one of our most basic educational necessities; the need to produce thoughtful, engaged, and compassionate human beings.
passages.zh: 支持创办微型学院的最终理由，是坚信我们每个人都要通过与那些了解并关心我们的人密切互动，才能充分实现自身的人性；而高等教育的基本目的之一就是社会性目的。尽管我们口头上赞同大学教育会使我们成为更好的人，但归根结底，我们主要还是从经济角度看待高等教育。我们逐渐把高等教育视为谋生的手段，而不是创造生活的途径。我们也逐渐把高等教育看成一种私人利益，而非公共利益。微型学院并不能解决我们所有的教育需求，但它能够满足我们最基本的教育需要之一：培养有思想、积极参与社会且富有同情心的人。

statements.en: One tiny American college situated on a cattle farm is devoted to educating students to serve mankind throughout their lives.
statements.zh: 一所位于养牛场的美国小型学院致力于教育学生终生为人类服务。

analysis.锚点: 牧场 + 一生服务人类
analysis.定位: G 段 Located on a working cattle ranch on the California-Nevada border, Deep Springs is a private, residential, two-year college for men, committed to educating students for "a life of service to humanity." Deep Springs 学院坐落在加州与内华达州交界处一座仍在运营的牛牧场上，是一所私立、住宿制、为男生开办的两年制学院，致力于培养学生过一种服务于人类的人生。
analysis.改写: One tiny American college situated on a cattle farm↔Located on a working cattle ranch on the California-Nevada border, Deep Springs is a private, residential, two-year college for men 牧场与学院身份的同义对应 devoted to educating students to serve mankind throughout their lives↔committed to educating students for "a life of service to humanity." 宗旨表述的同义改写
analysis.辨邻: I I段同样在介绍一所小校 Sterling College，地点写明在Craftsbury Common, Vermont而非牧场，办学重心是environmental and social justice issues而不是终身服务人类，与题干两个核心锚点都对不上。 Sterling College, in Craftsbury Common, Vermont, is also very small—fewer than 100 students.

statements.en: Much to the author's disappointment, the three institutions of higher learning where she taught largely ignore students' growth as social beings.
statements.zh: 令作者大失所望的是,她任教的三所高等学府在很大程度上忽视了学生作为社会人的成长。

analysis.锚点: 三所高校 + 失望 + 忽视社会成长
analysis.定位: D 段 I've had the privilege of teaching at three different institutions of higher learning during my career—a small liberal arts college and two mid-sized public universities. I've also been profoundly disappointed in each of these institutions, and in many of my colleagues, especially when it comes to helping students and preparing them for the many responsibilities of adulthood. 我职业生涯中有幸在三所高等教育机构任教——一所小型文理学院和两所中等规模的公立大学。但我也对这三所机构以及很多同事深感失望，尤其是在帮助学生、为他们承担成人世界的诸多责任做准备这件事上。
analysis.改写: Much to the author's disappointment↔I've also been profoundly disappointed in each of these institutions 情绪程度词的同义改写 the three institutions of higher learning where she taught↔teaching at three different institutions of higher learning during my career 数字与机构身份原样复现 largely ignore students' growth as social beings↔Little deliberate attention is given to how students mature as individuals and social beings 忽视社会成长的同义改写
analysis.辨邻: E E段同样是作者第一人称叙述，但讲的是退休后回家乡to establish a tiny college这件建设性的事，并没有出现题干所说的失望情绪，也没有提及作者教过的三所学校忽视学生社会成长这一事实。 Having just retired from teaching at a public university, I'm now returning to my hometown of Flagstaff, Arizona, to establish a tiny college—Flagstaff College.

statements.en: Tiny colleges must be made affordable in order to play a role in higher education.
statements.zh: 小型学院必须做到经济上可负担,才能在高等教育中发挥作用。

analysis.锚点: 可负担 + 在高等教育中起作用
analysis.定位: J 段 If tiny schools are to become a player on the higher education scene, they will need to find a way to be truly affordable. 如果微型大学想成为高等教育领域里的一员，它们必须找到一种真正能让人负担得起的办法。
analysis.改写: Tiny colleges must be made affordable↔they will need to find a way to be truly affordable 情态动词与被动表达的等值改写 in order to play a role in higher education↔If tiny schools are to become a player on the higher education scene 条件状语与目的状语的句式重构
analysis.辨邻: K K段谈的是什么因素drives up the cost of education，属于解释为什么高校学费高，但并没有像题干那样下出微型大学要扮演角色就必须可负担这一条件断言，话题相邻但论点不同。 All of this drives up the cost of education.

statements.en: According to a recent graduate from a tiny college, living together with faculty and fellow students is conducive to a student's growth as a person.
statements.zh: 据一位小型学院的应届毕业生说,与教师和同学共同生活有助于学生的个人成长。

analysis.锚点: 近毕业生 + 与师生共同生活
analysis.定位: H 段 "Living in close community with one's teachers and fellow students, and being forced to take on adult responsibilities, makes for one's growth as a person," says William Hunt, who graduated last year. 去年刚毕业的 William Hunt 说：与老师和同学紧密生活在一起，并被迫承担成人责任，会促成一个人作为人的成长。
analysis.改写: According to a recent graduate from a tiny college↔says William Hunt, who graduated last year 说话人身份的同义改写 living together with faculty and fellow students is conducive to a student's growth as a person↔Living in close community with one's teachers and fellow students, and being forced to take on adult responsibilities, makes for one's growth as a person 共同生活促进成长的同义改写

statements.en: Rather than going small, most American universities are trying to go big.
statements.zh: 大多数美国大学并非走小型化路线,而是试图走大型化路线。

analysis.锚点: 多数美国大学反而做大
analysis.定位: B 段 In higher education the trend is mostly in the opposite direction: Universities with 20,000 or 30,000 students are considered "mid-sized". The nation's largest university, Arizona State University, has 80,000 students on campus and aims to enroll another 100,000 students online. 在高等教育领域，趋势却大体相反：拥有两三万学生的大学被视为中等规模；全美最大的亚利桑那州立大学校园里有八万名学生，并计划再招十万名网课学生。
analysis.改写: Rather than going small↔In higher education the trend is mostly in the opposite direction 反方向的同义改写 most American universities are trying to go big↔Universities with 20,000 or 30,000 students are considered "mid-sized". The nation's largest university, Arizona State University, has 80,000 students on campus and aims to enroll another 100,000 students online. 具象数字向抽象趋势的归纳
analysis.辨邻: A A段谈的是社会层面上the rebirth of smallness，主语是农夫市集与精酿小店这类小事物，正在被赞颂——与题干说大学在做大方向相反，且主体也不是大学。 We're experiencing the rebirth of smallness.

statements.en: In a certain tiny college, rigorous academic work and traditional manual labor are integrated.
statements.zh: 在某所小型学院,严谨的学术工作与传统的体力劳动相结合。

analysis.锚点: 严肃学术 + 传统体力劳动
analysis.定位: I 段 According to its catalog, a college education at Sterling combines "rigorous academics, roll-up-your-sleeves challenges, and good old hard work." 据学校简章介绍，在 Sterling 接受的大学教育融合了严苛的学术、挽起袖子真干的挑战，以及踏踏实实的体力劳动。
analysis.改写: rigorous academic work and traditional manual labor are integrated↔a college education at Sterling combines "rigorous academics, roll-up-your-sleeves challenges, and good old hard work." 整合关系与并列项的等值改写 traditional manual labor↔it places a high value on personal responsibility and manual labor 传统体力劳动在该段被原样命名
analysis.辨邻: G G段同样谈到学术与劳动，但用的是academics, labor, and self-governance这一三件套——多了 self-governance、没有 rigorous 这一修饰，也没有 manual labor 这一具体表述，与题干强调的严苛学术 + 传统体力劳动对不上。 Deep Springs "curriculum" revolves around academics, labor, and self-governance.

statements.en: Tiny colleges focus on educating students to become well-rounded citizens instead of seeking their own expansion.
statements.zh: 小型学院专注于将学生培养成全面发展的公民,而不是谋求自身扩张。

analysis.锚点: 全人公民 PK 机构扩张
analysis.定位: C 段 They replace concerns about institutional growth with attention to the growth of students as fully developed participants in their communities. 微型大学用关注学生成长（让他们成为社区里全面发展的成员）取代了对机构本身扩张的关切。
analysis.改写: focus on educating students to become well-rounded citizens↔attention to the growth of students as fully developed participants in their communities 全人公民与全面发展成员的同义改写 instead of seeking their own expansion↔They replace concerns about institutional growth with attention to the growth of students 对照关系的句式重构
analysis.辨邻: M M段虽然也在为微型大学辩护，但论点是the need to help young people transition into adulthood目前几乎被完全忽视，并没有像题干那样把全面发展公民与机构扩张做出明确对照。 But I'm now convinced there's an educational need that's now going almost completely unmet

statements.en: The essence of education lies in the interaction between people.
statements.zh: 教育的本质在于人与人之间的互动。

analysis.定位: L 段 At its core, education is a human-to-human interaction. 教育在本质上是一种人与人之间的互动。
analysis.改写: The essence of education lies in the interaction between people↔At its core, education is a human-to-human interaction. 本质判断与 to be 句的等值改写
analysis.辨邻: N N段强调close interaction with those who know and care for us让我们成为完整的人，谈的是亲近之人的互动如何造就人性，而不是题干所说教育的本质是什么这一定义式判断。 each of us comes into our full humanity by close interaction with those who know and care for us

statements.en: After her retirement, the author has decided to set up a tiny college in her hometown.
statements.zh: 退休后,作者决定在家乡创办一所小型学院。

analysis.锚点: 退休 + 家乡 + 办微校
analysis.定位: E 段 Having just retired from teaching at a public university, I'm now returning to my hometown of Flagstaff, Arizona, to establish a tiny college—Flagstaff College. 我刚刚从公立大学教职上退休，正回到家乡亚利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫去创办一所微型大学——Flagstaff College。
analysis.改写: After her retirement↔Having just retired from teaching at a public university 时间状语与分词结构的等值改写 set up a tiny college in her hometown↔returning to my hometown of Flagstaff, Arizona, to establish a tiny college 创办与回归的同义改写
analysis.辨邻: D D段讲的是作者过去的任教经历I've had the privilege of teaching at three different institutions of higher learning during my career，并没有提到题干所说的退休后才发生的创办家乡微校这件事。 I've had the privilege of teaching at three different institutions of higher learning during my career

statements.en: Tiny colleges are justified as it is believed that our growth into full humanity comes through interaction with people near and dear to us.
statements.zh: 小型学院之所以合理,是因为人们相信我们成长为完整的人是通过与身边亲近之人的互动实现的。

analysis.锚点: 靠亲近之人的互动而成人
analysis.定位: N 段 The ultimate justification for a tiny college is the conviction that each of us comes into our full humanity by close interaction with those who know and care for us, and that one of the basic purposes of higher education is social. 微型大学最终的正当性在于这样一种信念：我们每个人都是通过与那些了解我们、关爱我们的人之间的紧密互动，才进入完整的人性；高等教育最根本的目的之一是社会性的。
analysis.改写: Tiny colleges are justified as it is believed that↔The ultimate justification for a tiny college is the conviction that 辩护与信念表达的等值改写 our growth into full humanity comes through interaction with people near and dear to us↔each of us comes into our full humanity by close interaction with those who know and care for us 成人途径的同义改写
analysis.辨邻: L L段虽然也讲education is a human-to-human interaction，但停留在教育本质这一定义层，并没有像题干那样把这一互动表述为微型大学的最终辩护。 At its core, education is a human-to-human interaction.

reading1.title: 2023年6月·第3套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 1 篇 · 46–50 题答案与解析

passages.en: If you're someone who has turned to snacking on junk food more in the pandemic(大流行病), you're not alone. Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances. His 2013 book, Salt Sugar Fat, explored food companies' aggressive marketing of those products and their impact on our health. In his new book, Hooked, Moss updates the food giants' efforts to keep us eating what they serve, and how they're responding to complaints from consumers and health advocates.
passages.zh: 如果你是在这场大流行病期间转而更多地吃垃圾食品的人，那么你并不孤单。调查记者迈克尔·莫斯说，加工食品经过精心设计，会让你上瘾，这与酒精、香烟或其他有害物质并无二致。他2013年出版的《盐、糖、脂肪》一书探讨了食品公司对这些产品的激进营销及其对我们健康的影响。在他的新书《上瘾》中，莫斯进一步介绍了食品巨头为让我们继续食用它们所提供的食品而采取的措施，以及它们如何回应消费者和健康倡导者的投诉。

passages.en: Processed food is inexpensive, it's legal, and it's everywhere. Companies' advertising is cueing us to remember those products and we want those products constantly. So the food environment is one of those key things that makes food even more problematic for so many people. Memory, nostalgia(怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave. Soda companies discovered that if they put a soda in the hands of a child when they're at a ball game with their parents, that soda will forever be associated with that joyous moment. Later in life, when that child wants to experience a joyous moment, they're going to think of soda. Many people seek comfort in the snacks they remember from childhood.
passages.zh: 加工食品价格低廉、合法，而且无处不在。公司的广告不断给我们提示，让我们记住这些产品，而我们也总是想要这些产品。因此，对许多人来说，食品环境是使食物问题变得更加严重的关键因素之一。记忆，尤其是怀旧，在我们渴望的食物中发挥着重要作用。汽水公司发现，如果他们在孩子和父母一起观看球赛时把一瓶汽水递到孩子手中，那么这瓶汽水将永远与那个欢乐时刻联系在一起。这个孩子长大后，当他想体验欢乐时刻时，就会想到汽水。许多人会从儿时记忆中的零食中寻求慰藉。

passages.en: Moss examines the way companies capitalize on our memories, cravings and brain chemistry to keep us snacking.
passages.zh: 莫斯考察了食品公司如何利用我们的记忆、渴望和大脑化学机制，让我们不停地吃零食。

passages.en: One of the reasons I came to think that some of these food products are even more powerful, more troublesome than drugs can be is memory. What we eat is all about memory. And we begin forming memories for food at a really early age. And we keep those memories for a lifetime. Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products. One of the features of addiction that scientists studying drug addiction discovered back in the 1990s was that the faster a substance hits the brain, the more apt we are as a result to act impulsively. There's nothing faster than food in its ability to hit the brain. For Moss, this puts the notion of "fast food" in an entirely new light as this isn't limited to fast food chains-almost 90% of food products in grocery stores are processed foods. Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.
passages.zh: 我之所以开始认为其中一些食品甚至比毒品更有力量、更令人苦恼，原因之一就是记忆。我们吃什么，全都与记忆有关。而且，我们在很小的时候就开始形成关于食物的记忆，并会将这些记忆保留一生。食品行业深知这一点，因此花费大量时间试图塑造我们对其产品的记忆。20世纪90年代，研究毒品成瘾的科学家发现，成瘾的一个特征是，一种物质越快作用于大脑，我们随后就越容易冲动行事。没有什么比食物作用于大脑的速度更快。对莫斯来说，这让“快餐”这一概念有了全新的含义，因为这并不局限于快餐连锁店——杂货店中近90%的食品都是加工食品。从生产到包装，这个行业的一切都与速度有关。

passages.en: Overall, Moss outlines the industry's dependence on making their products inexpensive, super delicious, and incredibly convenient for consumers. Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.
passages.zh: 总的来说，莫斯概述了这个行业对以下做法的依赖：让产品价格低廉、极其美味，并为消费者提供难以置信的便利。如今，越来越多的人开始关注自己摄入的东西，并希望吃得更健康，而由于这些公司自身沉迷于生产这类便利食品，它们发现要满足这种新的需求非常困难。

questions.stem: In what way does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes?
questions.stem_zh: Michael Moss 认为加工食品在哪方面可与酒精和香烟相提并论?

options.text: They are all addictive.
options.zh: 它们都会使人上瘾。

options.text: They are all necessary evils.
options.zh: 它们都是必要之恶。

options.text: They are all engineered to be enjoyed.
options.zh: 它们都经过设计以让人享受。

options.text: They are all in increasingly great demand.
options.zh: 它们的需求都在日益增长。

questions.判型: In what way does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes? 问的是一个明确的可比关系，答案应能从原文一句话直接读出。
questions.拆句: 主干 does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes，从句 that 省略，理解关键是 comparable to 的语义"与……可比"，不是"被比作"。结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances. 调查记者 Michael Moss 说，加工食品被精心设计来"勾住"你，这一点与酒精、香烟或其他有害物质并无不同。

locate.en: Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances.
locate.zh: 调查记者 Michael Moss 说，加工食品被精心设计来"勾住"你，这一点与酒精、香烟或其他有害物质并无不同。

option_analysis.note: 预判"勾住人"对应 addictive，A 即为对定位句双重否定+动词短语的整体重述。

pairs.orig: not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances

option_analysis.note: necessary evils 原文未提及；Moss 全文批评加工食品，没有任何"必要"评价。
engineered to be enjoyed 把原文 engineered to hook you 偷换为"为享受而设计"——hook 是"勾住、使上瘾"的强迫语义，与"被享受"的中性愉悦语义不等。
increasingly great demand 原文未提及"需求日益增大"；Moss 说的是公司在"积极推销"（aggressive marketing），不是消费者需求暴涨。

questions.stem: What does the author say plays a key role in the foods we crave?
questions.stem_zh: 作者认为什么在我们渴望的食物中起着关键作用?

options.text: The food environment.

options.text: Memory.
options.zh: 记忆。

questions.判型: What does the author say plays a key role in the foods we crave? 问的是某个明确因素，答案是原文里一句陈述句的主语或表语。
questions.拆句: What does the author say plays a key role in the foods we crave? 中 What 既是 say 的宾语从句的主语、又是 plays 的主语；the foods we crave 是省略了 that 的定语从句。结构标准、无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 Memory, nostalgia(怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave. 记忆，尤其是怀旧情感，在我们渴求的食物中起着举足轻重的作用。

locate.en: Memory, nostalgia(怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave.
locate.zh: 记忆，尤其是怀旧情感，在我们渴求的食物中起着举足轻重的作用。

questions.stem: What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers' association with their food products?
questions.stem_zh: 食品公司如何利用消费者对其食品产品的联想?

options.text: They strive to influence how consumers remember their products.
options.zh: 它们努力影响消费者对其产品的记忆方式。

options.text: They attempt to use consumers' long-term memories to promote addiction.
options.zh: 它们试图利用消费者的长期记忆来促进成瘾。

options.text: They try to exploit consumers' memories for their products as early as possible.
options.zh: 它们试图尽早利用消费者对其产品的记忆。

options.text: They endeavor to find what consumers remember about their products.
options.zh: 它们努力找出消费者对其产品的记忆内容。

questions.判型: What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers' association with their food products? 问的是公司具体做了什么，是原文动作的同义改写。
questions.拆句: What do food companies do to capitalize on consumers' association with their food products? 中 to capitalize on... 是目的状语；consumers' association with... 是"消费者对……的联想"。结构清晰、无陷阱。
questions.定位: P4 Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products. 明白这一点之后，食品行业花费大量时间，努力塑造我们对其产品所留存的记忆。

locate.en: Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products.
locate.zh: 明白这一点之后，食品行业花费大量时间，努力塑造我们对其产品所留存的记忆。

option_analysis.note: 预判的"塑造记忆"与 influence how consumers remember 在动作（塑造/影响）和对象（记忆/如何记住）上双重对应。

pairs.orig: trying to shape the memories that we have for their products
pairs.opt: strive to influence how consumers remember their products

option_analysis.note: use consumers' long-term memories to promote addiction 把"塑造记忆"曲解为"利用长期记忆推动成瘾"——原文虽然提到 features of addiction，但其语境是说"食物入脑速度快"，并不是把记忆当成瘾工具。
exploit consumers' memories for their products as early as possible 把动作偷换为"尽早利用记忆"，并嫁接首段 we begin forming memories for food at a really early age 的"早期"细节——但原文说的是"消费者从小开始形成记忆"，不是"公司尽早去利用"。
endeavor to find what consumers remember about their products 把"塑造（shape）"偷换为"查明（find）"——前者是主动改变记忆，后者是被动调查记忆，方向完全相反。

questions.stem: How does the food industry operate from manufacturing to packaging, according to Moss?
questions.stem_zh: 根据 Moss 的说法,食品行业从生产到包装是如何运作的?

options.text: Placing the idea of fast food in an entirely new light.
options.zh: 将快餐的概念置于全新的视角。

options.text: Setting no limit to the number of fast food chains.
options.zh: 对快餐连锁店的数量不设限制。

options.text: Focusing on how quickly the work is done.
options.zh: 专注于工作完成的速度。

options.text: Prioritizing the quality of their products.
options.zh: 优先考虑其产品的质量。

questions.判型: How does the food industry operate from manufacturing to packaging, according to Moss? 问的是"以什么方式运作"，答案是原文一句话的同义改写。
questions.拆句: How does the food industry operate from manufacturing to packaging, according to Moss? 中 from...to... 是状语，according to Moss 是引述来源。结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。
questions.定位: P4 Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging. 整个行业的一切都围绕"速度"展开，从生产到包装无一例外。

locate.en: Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.
locate.zh: 整个行业的一切都围绕"速度"展开，从生产到包装无一例外。

option_analysis.note: Placing the idea of fast food in an entirely new light 是 Moss 对"fast food"概念的重新解读结果，对应 this puts the notion of "fast food" in an entirely new light，但 Q49 问的是行业"如何运作"，不是 Moss"如何看待 fast food 概念"。
Setting no limit to the number of fast food chains 来自对 isn't limited to fast food chains 的曲解——原文是说"fast food 不限于连锁快餐店（含义=加工食品也算 fast food）"，不是说"快餐连锁店数量没有上限"。
预判的"以速度为核心"与 Focusing on how quickly the work is done 在核心概念上完全等值。

pairs.orig: Everything in the industry is about speed
pairs.opt: Focusing on how quickly the work is done

option_analysis.note: Prioritizing the quality of their products 说"优先考虑质量"，但原文明确说 Everything in the industry is about speed——是"速度"优先，不是"质量"优先。

questions.stem: Why are companies finding it difficult to satisfy consumers' demand for healthier food products?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么公司发现难以满足消费者对更健康食品的需求?

options.text: They think speed of production outweighs consumers' health.
options.zh: 它们认为生产速度比消费者健康更重要。

options.text: They believe their industry would perish without fast foods.
options.zh: 它们相信没有快餐其行业将会消亡。

options.text: They have to strike a balance between taste and nutrition.
options.zh: 它们必须在口味和营养之间取得平衡。

options.text: They are hooked on manufacturing convenience foods.
options.zh: 它们沉迷于生产方便食品。

questions.判型: Why are companies finding it difficult to satisfy consumers' demand for healthier food products? 问的是直接原因，原文必有 because/due to 之类的因果句对应。
questions.拆句: Why are companies finding it difficult to satisfy consumers' demand for healthier food products? 中 finding it difficult to V 是"find + it（形式宾语）+ difficult + 不定式真宾语"结构；考生若把 it 当作普通代词指代前文事物，就会读偏。
questions.定位: P5 Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods. 如今越来越多的人在意吃进体内的东西、想吃得更健康，这些公司发现自己很难满足这一新需求，原因在于它们自身已经"上瘾"于生产这些便利食品。

locate.en: Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.
locate.zh: 如今越来越多的人在意吃进体内的东西、想吃得更健康，这些公司发现自己很难满足这一新需求，原因在于它们自身已经"上瘾"于生产这些便利食品。

option_analysis.note: speed of production outweighs consumers' health 把第四段"速度优先"与末段"难满足健康需求"硬串成因果——原文确实说过 about speed，但并未说"速度压倒健康"是公司难以满足新需求的原因。
their industry would perish without fast foods 完全是凭空想象，原文未涉及行业"消亡"或"存亡"。
strike a balance between taste and nutrition 把末段 super delicious 和 eat healthier 硬凑成"口味与营养的平衡"——但原文没有任何"平衡"的表述，给出的真正原因是公司自身"上瘾"。
预判的"对制造便利食品上瘾"与 hooked on manufacturing convenience foods 完全等值，且 hooked on 回扣首段 hook 一词，是作者刻意的呼应。

pairs.orig: their own addiction to making these convenience foods

reading2.title: 2023年6月·第3套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: Chimpanzees(黑猩猩), human beings' closest animal relatives, share up to 98% of our genes. Yet humans and chimpanzees lead very different lives. Fewer than 300,000 wild chimpanzees live in a few forested corners of Africa today, while humans have colonized every corner of the globe. At more than 7 billion, human population dwarfs that of nearly all other mammals—despite our physical weaknesses.
passages.zh: 黑猩猩作为人类最亲近的动物近亲，与人类共享高达98%的基因。然而，人类和黑猩猩过着截然不同的生活。如今，只有不到30万只野生黑猩猩生活在非洲少数覆盖森林的角落，而人类则拓展到了地球的每一个角落。尽管我们在体质上存在弱点，但超过70亿的人口数量使几乎所有其他哺乳动物都相形见绌。

passages.en: What could account for our species' incredible evolutionary successes?
passages.zh: 究竟是什么能够解释我们这一物种令人难以置信的演化成功？

passages.en: One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.
passages.zh: 一个显而易见的答案是我们庞大的大脑。可能是我们的原始智力赋予了我们前所未有的打破常规思考的能力，使人们在向全球迁移的过程中能够创新出解决棘手问题的方案。

passages.en: But a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists(人类学家) are rejecting that explanation. They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.
passages.zh: 但越来越多的认知科学家和人类学家正在否定这一解释。他们认为，我们之所以能够生存和繁衍，恰恰是因为我们没有独立思考，而不是依靠成为创新者来谋生。相反，人们通过仔细模仿他人来应对具有挑战性的气候和生态环境。

passages.en: In a famous study, psychologists Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten showed two groups of test subjects—children and chimpanzees—a mechanical box with a treat inside. In one condition, the box was opaque, while in the other it was transparent. The experimenters demonstrated how to open the box to retrieve the treat, but they also included the irrelevant step of tapping on the box with a stick.
passages.zh: 在一项著名的研究中，心理学家维多利亚·霍纳和安德鲁·怀腾向两组受试者——儿童和黑猩猩——展示了一个里面装有奖励的机械盒。在一种情况下，盒子是不透明的，而在另一种情况下，盒子则是透明的。实验人员演示了如何打开盒子取回奖励，但他们也包含了一个无关紧要的步骤：用棍子敲击盒子。

passages.en: Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.
passages.zh: 奇怪的是，孩子们仔细地复制了打开盒子的所有步骤，即使他们能看到棍子没有任何实际作用。也就是说，他们进行了非理性的模仿：孩子们盲目地模仿了他们所目睹的每一个动作，而不是只做获得奖励所必需的事情。

passages.en: Of course, that study only included three—and four-year-olds. But additional research has shown that older children and adults are even more likely to mindlessly copy others' actions, and infants are less likely to over-imitate—that is, to precisely copy even impractical actions.
passages.zh: 当然，该研究仅包含三岁和四岁的儿童。但进一步的研究表明，大龄儿童和成年人更有可能盲目地模仿他人的行为，而婴儿则不太可能过度模仿——即精确复制哪怕是不切实际的动作。

passages.en: By contrast, chimpanzees in the study only over-imitated in the opaque condition. In the transparent condition—where they saw that the stick was mechanically useless—they ignored that step entirely. Other research has since supported these findings.
passages.zh: 相比之下，研究中的黑猩猩仅在不透明的情况下才会过度模仿。在透明的情况下——当它们看到棍子在机械上毫无用处时——它们完全忽略了那个步骤。此后的其他研究也支持了这些发现。

passages.en: When it comes to copying, chimpanzees are more rational than human children or adults.
passages.zh: 在模仿方面，黑猩猩比人类儿童或成年人更理性。

passages.en: Where does the seemingly irrational human preference for over-imitation come from? Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers.
passages.zh: 人类对过度模仿的这种看似非理性的偏好究竟来自何处？人类学家约瑟夫·亨里奇指出，世界各地的人们所依赖的技术往往非常复杂，以至于没有任何人能够理性地学会它们。相反，人们必须一步一步地学习它们，信任更有经验的长者和平辈的智慧。

passages.en: So the next time you hear someone arguing passionately that everyone should embrace nonconformity and avoid imitating others, you might laugh a little bit. We're not chimpanzees, after all.
passages.zh: 因此，下次当你听到有人慷慨激昂地主张每个人都应该追求特立独行、避免模仿他人时，你可能会微微一笑。毕竟，我们不是黑猩猩。

questions.stem: What might explain humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals?
questions.stem_zh: 什么可能解释人类拥有几乎所有哺乳动物中最大的种群数量?

options.text: They are equipped with raw strength for solving the most challenging problems.
options.zh: 他们具备解决最具挑战性问题的原始力量。

options.text: They cope with the outside world more effectively than their animal relatives.
options.zh: 他们比动物亲缘物种更有效地应对外部世界。

options.text: They possess the most outstanding ability to think.
options.zh: 他们拥有最杰出的思考能力。

options.text: They know how to survive everywhere on earth.
options.zh: 他们知道如何在地球上任何地方生存。

questions.判型: 题干 What might explain humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals? 指向文章中给出原因解释的某一句，并非全文主旨，属于细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干是 What might explain X，其中 X 由动名词短语 humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals 充当 explain 的宾语；不定式般的动名词结构是六级常见考点，注意 humans' 是 having 的逻辑主语，不是 population 的所有格。
questions.定位: P3 One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe. 一个显而易见的答案是我们的大脑。可能是我们的纯粹智力赋予了我们一种前所未有的跳出思维定式的能力，让人们在迁徙到全球各处时能够创新性地解决棘手难题。

locate.en: One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.
locate.zh: 一个显而易见的答案是我们的大脑。可能是我们的纯粹智力赋予了我们一种前所未有的跳出思维定式的能力，让人们在迁徙到全球各处时能够创新性地解决棘手难题。

option_analysis.note: 选项 equipped with raw strength for solving the most challenging problems 用 raw strength 替换原文 raw intelligence，正话反说——文章首段恰恰强调 despite our physical weaknesses，人类身体反而是弱的。

They cope with the outside world more effectively than their animal relatives 用 animal relatives 把题点引向 Chimpanzees, human beings' closest animal relatives——黑猩猩，但 51 题问的是 largest population of almost all mammals 的原因，原因句在 P3 而非 P1。
预判已锁定卓越的思考能力，C 选项 possess the most outstanding ability to think 在词面与语义上都与定位句一一对应，是定位句的标准同义替换。

pairs.opt: possess the most outstanding ability to think

option_analysis.note: They know how to survive everywhere on earth 是 humans have colonized every corner of the globe 的同义改写，但这是现象本身，不是题目所问的解释；题干 What might explain 要的是 原因。

questions.stem: What accounts for humans' evolutionary successes according to a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists?
questions.stem_zh: 根据越来越多认知科学家和人类学家的观点,什么解释了人类进化的成功?

options.text: They are better at innovating solutions.
options.zh: 他们更擅长创新解决方案。

options.text: They thrive through creative strategies.
options.zh: 他们通过创造性策略繁荣发展。

options.text: They are naturally adaptive to ecological contexts.
options.zh: 他们天生适应生态环境。

options.text: They meet challenges by imitating others carefully.
options.zh: 他们通过仔细模仿他人来应对挑战。

questions.判型: 题干 according to a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists 限定了观点来源，要求回原文找到该群体说了什么，属典型署名细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干 What accounts for humans' evolutionary successes，后接 according to 短语作状语限定信息来源；account for 在此意为解释/导致，是六级高频熟词僻义。
questions.定位: P4 They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others. 他们认为：我们之所以存活下来并蓬勃发展，恰恰不是因为我们以创新者的身份谋生，而恰恰是因为我们不自己思考。相反，人类是通过仔细地模仿他人来应对极具挑战的气候与生态环境的。

locate.en: They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.
locate.zh: 他们认为：我们之所以存活下来并蓬勃发展，恰恰不是因为我们以创新者的身份谋生，而恰恰是因为我们不自己思考。相反，人类是通过仔细地模仿他人来应对极具挑战的气候与生态环境的。

option_analysis.note: They are better at innovating solutions 来自 innovating solutions to thorny problems——但这是 P4 But 转折之前被驳的旧解释，不是 a growing number of 科学家的观点；题干限定了观点出处，必须取转折之后。
They thrive through creative strategies 用 creative——这与 we don't think for ourselves 直接相反，文章明确说人类成功不靠自己思考创新。
They are naturally adaptive to ecological contexts 把 ecological contexts 抄过来制造熟悉感，但 naturally adaptive（与生俱来的适应性）这种说法在原文没有任何出处——文章强调的是后天模仿。
预判已锁定靠仔细模仿来应对挑战，They meet challenges by imitating others carefully 在结构（meet challenges by + 动名词短语）和措辞上与定位句完全同义。

pairs.orig: cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts

questions.stem: What does the author think is odd about the findings of the study by Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten?
questions.stem_zh: 作者认为Victoria Horner和Andrew Whiten的研究发现有什么奇怪之处?

options.text: Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters.
options.zh: 儿童非理性地模仿了实验者的每一个动作。

options.text: Chimpanzees could tell the transparent box from the opaque one.
options.zh: 黑猩猩能够区分透明盒子和不透明盒子。

options.text: Chimpanzees could retrieve the treat more quickly than children did.
options.zh: 黑猩猩取得奖励的速度比儿童更快。

options.text: Children omitted the step of tapping on the box with a stick to open it.
options.zh: 儿童省略了用棍子敲击盒子以打开它的步骤。

questions.判型: 题干问的是作者认为某项研究中 odd 的具体内容，需要回到原文一句话找出对应描述，是细节题而非态度题。
questions.拆句: 主干 What does the author think is odd about X，think 后跟省略 that 的宾语从句 is odd about the findings，about 短语限定 odd 的范围；考生易把 think is odd 误读成主旨态度题。
questions.定位: P6 Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed. 奇怪的是，儿童仔细地模仿了开盒子的每一步动作，哪怕他们能看出那根木棒并没有任何实际作用。也就是说，他们的模仿是非理性的：他们没有只做获得奖励所必需的动作，而是奴隶般地模仿了所看到的每一个动作。

locate.en: Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.
locate.zh: 奇怪的是，儿童仔细地模仿了开盒子的每一步动作，哪怕他们能看出那根木棒并没有任何实际作用。也就是说，他们的模仿是非理性的：他们没有只做获得奖励所必需的动作，而是奴隶般地模仿了所看到的每一个动作。

option_analysis.note: A 选项 Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters 完整对应定位句的两个关键点：irrationally 对应 slavishly/irrationally，every action of the experimenters 对应 every action they'd witnessed。

pairs.orig: children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed
pairs.opt: Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters

option_analysis.note: Chimpanzees could tell the transparent box from the opaque one 描述黑猩猩能区分透明与不透明盒子——这是 P8 黑猩猩对比段的隐含信息，但题干问的是作者认为 odd 的发现，奇怪在儿童这边，不在黑猩猩能不能区分上。
Chimpanzees could retrieve the treat more quickly than children did 提到黑猩猩比儿童更快取得食物——这种速度比较在文中没有任何描写。
Children omitted the step of tapping on the box with a stick to open it 说儿童跳过了敲打这一步——与 children carefully copied all the steps 完全相反，且 P8 显示是黑猩猩在透明条件下才跳过这一步。

questions.stem: What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying?
questions.stem_zh: 人类学家Joseph Henrich对人类偏好模仿的解释是什么?

options.text: It originates in the rationality of people around the world.
options.zh: 它源于世界各地人们的理性。

options.text: It stems from the way people learn complex technologies.
options.zh: 它源于人们学习复杂技术的方式。

options.text: It results from people distrusting their own wisdom.
options.zh: 它源于人们不信任自己的智慧。

options.text: It derives from the desire to acquire knowledge step by step.
options.zh: 它源于逐步获取知识的愿望。

questions.判型: 题干 What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying? 明确指向某专家对某行为的解释，属于署名+原因型细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干 What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying，anthropologist 是 Joseph Henrich 的同位语；preference for copying 名词化结构相当于 prefer to copy。
questions.定位: P10 Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers. 人类学家 Joseph Henrich 指出：世界各地的人都依赖于一些非常复杂的技术，复杂到没有人能够完全理性地学会它们。因此，人们必须一步一步地学习这些技术，并信任那些更有经验的前辈与同伴的智慧。

locate.en: Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers.
locate.zh: 人类学家 Joseph Henrich 指出：世界各地的人都依赖于一些非常复杂的技术，复杂到没有人能够完全理性地学会它们。因此，人们必须一步一步地学习这些技术，并信任那些更有经验的前辈与同伴的智慧。

option_analysis.note: It originates in the rationality of people around the world 说模仿源于人们的理性——可文中明确说 no one can learn them rationally，恰恰是 没法理性学 才需要模仿；选项把因果反过来了。
B It stems from the way people learn complex technologies 把 Henrich 的两步因果（技术复杂 → 必须一步步模仿）压缩成 模仿源于学习复杂技术的方式，与预判完全吻合。

pairs.orig: people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers
pairs.opt: It stems from the way people learn complex technologies

pairs.orig: technologies that are often so complex

option_analysis.note: It results from people distrusting their own wisdom——文章里只有 trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers，即信任 前辈与同伴 的智慧，并未说 不信任自己的智慧；distrust their own 是过度推断 + 与原文相反的合成。
It derives from the desire to acquire knowledge step by step 把 step by step 抄过来，但说成 是因为人有一步步获取知识的欲望——文章是说 因为技术太复杂、不得不 一步步学习，并不是出于 欲望。手段被替换成动机。

questions.stem: What point does the author want to emphasize when he says "We're not chimpanzees"?
questions.stem_zh: 当作者说"我们不是黑猩猩"时,他想强调什么观点?

options.text: It is arguable whether everyone should avoid imitation.
options.zh: 每个人是否都应该避免模仿是有争议的。

options.text: It is characteristic of human beings to copy others.
options.zh: 模仿他人是人类的特征。

options.text: It is desirable to trust in more knowledgeable peers.
options.zh: 信任更有知识的同伴是可取的。

options.text: It is naive to laugh at someone embracing nonconformity.
options.zh: 嘲笑拥抱不从众的人是幼稚的。

questions.判型: What point does the author want to emphasize 询问的是作者借这句反语想强调什么，属典型推断题。
questions.拆句: 题干主干 What point does the author want to emphasize when he says "We're not chimpanzees"?，when 引导时间状语从句，指明这句话所在的语境；需要把 not chimpanzees 当作对照、推出人类的特征。

option_analysis.note: It is arguable whether everyone should avoid imitation 把作者的话理解为 模仿是否该避免是个值得讨论的问题——但作者并没有在讨论 是否该避免，而是直接调侃那些反模仿者；arguable（有争议的）是无中生有的态度。
B It is characteristic of human beings to copy others 恰好把反语还原为正面陈述：模仿是人类的特征；其余三项要么没抓到反语指向、要么停留在字面。

pairs.opt: It is characteristic of human beings to copy others

option_analysis.note: It is desirable to trust in more knowledgeable peers 来自 trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers——这只是 Henrich 一段的局部解释，不是末段反语 We're not chimpanzees 想强调的点；末段强调的是 人类天性模仿，不是 信任前辈这件事好不好。
It is naive to laugh at someone embracing nonconformity 说嘲笑追求不从众的人是天真的——可文中作者恰恰说 you might laugh a little bit，即可以笑一笑，作者站的是支持嘲笑那一方；naive（天真的）正话反说。

translation.title: 2023年6月·第3套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 近年中国城市高质量发展与人居环境改善 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 近年来,中国城市加快发展,城市人居环境得到显著改善。许多城市努力探索中国特色的城市高质量发展之路,城市功能不断完善,治理水平明显提高。中国持续开展城市生态修复和功能修补,全面实施城镇老旧小区改造,大力推进城市园林绿化,消除污染 ;同时大力推进城市基础设施体系化建设,开展房屋建筑和市政设施普查以及安全隐患排查整治,努力为市民创造高品质的生活环境,让城市更美丽、更安全、更宜居。
translation.reference_en:
In recent years, Chinese cities have accelerated their development, and the urban living environment has improved significantly. Many cities strive to explore a path of high-quality urban development with Chinese characteristics, with urban functions being steadily improved and governance markedly enhanced. China has been carrying out a series of efforts, including the ecological restoration and functional improvement of cities, the comprehensive renovation of old urban residential communities, the vigorous promotion of urban landscaping and afforestation, and the elimination of pollution. At the same time, it vigorously advances the systematic construction of urban infrastructure and conducts surveys of housing and municipal facilities as well as the investigation and rectification of potential safety hazards, striving to create a high-quality living environment for citizens and to make cities more beautiful, safer and more livable.
【衔接】
第1、2句之间:用城市发展话题自然承接第1句讲 中国城市加快发展 这一总体局面,第2句 许多城市努力探索 落到具体城市的做法,是"总—分"承接。英文第2句以 Many cities 开头即可自然承接,无需强加关联词;若想显化,可在句首补 In particular 点出"具体而言"。
第3、4句之间:用 At the same time 显化并列中文原文 同时大力推进城市基础设施体系化建设 的"同时"是明确的并列/递进信号,英文务必译出 At the same time(或 Meanwhile)置于第4句首,把第3、4句两组举措并列起来;同时第4句主语用 it 承接第3句的 China,避免重复 China carries out/China advances 显得啰嗦。

cohesion.core: 第1、2句之间:用城市发展话题自然承接
cohesion.detail: 第1句讲 中国城市加快发展 这一总体局面,第2句 许多城市努力探索 落到具体城市的做法,是"总—分"承接。英文第2句以 Many cities 开头即可自然承接,无需强加关联词;若想显化,可在句首补 In particular 点出"具体而言"。

cohesion.core: 第3、4句之间:用 At the same time 显化并列
cohesion.detail: 中文原文 同时大力推进城市基础设施体系化建设 的"同时"是明确的并列/递进信号,英文务必译出 At the same time(或 Meanwhile)置于第4句首,把第3、4句两组举措并列起来;同时第4句主语用 it 承接第3句的 China,避免重复 China carries out/China advances 显得啰嗦。

main_idea.core: 近年中国城市高质量发展与人居环境改善
main_idea.detail: 全篇是一段客观介绍性陈述,讲近年来中国城市怎样发展、人居环境如何改善、采取了哪些具体举措。开篇 近年来,中国城市加快发展,城市人居环境得到显著改善 就把基调定为「陈述当下中国城市的发展现状与持续在做的工作」,既非历史叙事、也非个人观点,而是政府/媒体口径的成就介绍。这类「介绍中国社会发展」的文本正是六级汉译英的高频题材,语体偏正式、客观。

tense.detail: 通篇是对中国城市发展现状与持续性举措的客观陈述,描述的是「正在做、一直在做、已成常态」的事实而非某个已结束的历史事件。如 中国持续开展城市生态修复和功能修补 中的「持续开展」、城市功能不断完善 中的「不断」都指向「现在仍在进行的常态」,故全篇以一般现在时为默认基调;个别表「已取得的结果」处可酌情用现在完成时偏离。

term_notes.detail: 中国特色 是高频文化负载词,采用约定俗成的官方译法 with Chinese characteristics,作后置修饰,如「中国特色的城市高质量发展之路」译 a path of high-quality urban development with Chinese characteristics。全篇统一用此译法,不要自造 China's own style 之类。
城镇老旧小区改造 指对建成年代久、设施陈旧的居民住宅区进行翻新升级,意译为 the renovation of old urban residential communities;"老旧"译 old/aging,"小区"译 residential communities,"改造"译 renovation。

term_notes.core: 城市生态修复和功能修补
term_notes.detail: 城市生态修复和功能修补 是并列术语,"生态修复"译 ecological restoration,"功能修补"译 functional improvement/repair,合译 urban ecological restoration and functional improvement,全篇保持此译法。
市政设施 指道路、管网、公共照明等城市公用设施,统一译 municipal facilities;与之相关的"城市基础设施"译 urban infrastructure,二者区分开、各自固定。

steps.text: 两个分句各立主谓,后半转被动（主语策略：原句主语）本句含两层意思:前半 中国城市加快发展 主语是"中国城市"(Chinese cities),谓语"加快发展"译 have accelerated/sped up development;后半 城市人居环境得到显著改善 中文用"得到改善",承受动作的是"人居环境",故主干立为 the urban living environment has improved 或被动 has been significantly improved。

时间状语前置,两分句并列近年来 是时间状语,译 In recent years 置于句首;前后两个分句是"发展"带来"环境改善"的轻因果/并列关系,可用 and 连接两个独立主谓,或把后半处理为结果状语,如 ..., and the urban living environment has improved significantly。本句结构不复杂,降级幅度小,关键是两个分句各自主谓齐全、别拼成一个残句。

时态近年来 配"近年来"这一时间范围,表"过去延续到现在并已见成效",此处宜用现在完成时 have accelerated/has improved,这是对全篇一般现在时基调的合理偏离(时间状语 In recent years 触发完成时)。 单复数"中国城市"泛指众多城市,用复数 Chinese cities,相应谓语 have(复数);"城市人居环境"作整体不可数概念,用单数 the urban living environment has。 冠词特指"(中国的)城市人居环境"用定冠词 the urban living environment;"中国城市"作泛指复数主语,前面不加冠词。
In recent years, Chinese cities have accelerated their development, and the urban living environment has improved significantly.

主干 Many cities explore a path（主语策略：原句主语）本句核心动作是 许多城市努力探索...发展之路,主语"许多城市"(Many cities)、谓语"努力探索"(strive to explore/are exploring)、宾语"...发展之路"(a path of high-quality urban development with Chinese characteristics),以此立为主干。后两段 城市功能不断完善,治理水平明显提高 是探索带来的结果,降级处理。

后两分句降为结果状语城市功能不断完善,治理水平明显提高 是"探索发展之路"的伴随/结果,不宜再用 and 平铺成第三、第四个并列主谓。可改写为现在分词结果状语 ..., with urban functions being steadily improved and governance markedly enhanced,或用 as a result 引出;"中国特色"用后置介词短语 with Chinese characteristics 修饰 path,避免堆在名词前。

时态回指全篇基调,本句描述"现在正在做、持续在改善"的常态,用一般现在时 explore/strive to explore;"不断完善""明显提高"的状态也用现在时 are being improved/enhanced。 单复数"许多城市"用复数 Many cities,谓语 explore(复数);"城市功能"译复数 urban functions(功能不止一项)。 冠词"一条...发展之路"是泛指"一条道路",用不定冠词 a path of high-quality urban development。 用词"治理水平"译 governance(治理) 而非 management;"明显提高"用 markedly/significantly enhanced,程度副词别漏。
Many cities strive to explore a path of high-quality urban development with Chinese characteristics, with urban functions being steadily improved and governance markedly enhanced.
China + 并列谓语带多个宾语（主语策略：原句主语）本句主语明确是 中国(China),后面 持续开展城市生态修复和功能修补,全面实施城镇老旧小区改造,大力推进城市园林绿化,消除污染 是中国采取的一连串动作。主干立为 China carries out/has been carrying out,谓语用一个统领动词,后接多个并列宾语,而非逐个动作各立一句。

四个动作并列,动词降为动名词宾语本句是四个并列动作,英文可用 China carries out a series of efforts, including... 把后面四项处理成 including 引导的并列动名词/名词短语:ecological restoration and functional improvement, the renovation of old urban residential communities, urban landscaping and afforestation, and the elimination of pollution。"消除污染"译 eliminating pollution/the elimination of pollution,统一成名词/动名词形式与前面并列,别混入一个突兀的谓语。

时态持续开展 强调"持续、一直在做",用现在完成进行时 has been carrying out 最贴切;若取全篇一般现在时基调 carries out 亦可。二者择一,体现"持续性"即可。 主谓一致主语 China 是单数第三人称,谓语用 carries/has been(单数形式),别受后面一串复数宾语干扰写成 carry。 单复数"老旧小区"指多个住宅区,用复数 old urban residential communities;"污染"pollution 为不可数,不加 s。 用词"园林绿化"译 landscaping and afforestation(绿化/植树);"大力推进"用 vigorously promote/advance,程度词译出。

China has been carrying out a series of efforts, including the ecological restoration and functional improvement of cities, the comprehensive renovation of old urban residential communities, the vigorous promotion of urban landscaping and afforestation, and the elimination of pollution.
承前补主语 China/it（主语策略：补主语）本句中文承上句省略了主语,实际仍是"中国"在做。同时大力推进城市基础设施体系化建设 等四个动作需补出主语 China(或用 it 承接上句),主干为 it also vigorously advances/pushes forward,后接并列宾语;末尾 让城市更美丽、更安全、更宜居 是这些举措的目的/结果,降级处理。

前两动作并列,后两层降为目的状语大力推进城市基础设施体系化建设 与 开展房屋建筑和市政设施普查以及安全隐患排查整治 是两项并列举措,用 and 连接两个动名词/名词宾语;努力为市民创造高品质的生活环境 与 让城市更美丽、更安全、更宜居 是前面举措的目的,用不定式 to create a high-quality living environment for citizens and to make cities more beautiful, safer and more livable 作目的状语挂在句尾,而非再起两个并列谓语。

时态回指全篇基调与上句保持一致,用一般现在时/现在完成进行时 it also advances/has been advancing,与第3句同步,体现持续举措。 比较级"更美丽、更安全、更宜居"用比较级 more beautiful, safer and more livable;注意 safe 的比较级是 safer(单音节加 er),beautiful/livable 用 more,别统一套 more 写成 more safe。 介词搭配"为市民创造...环境"用 create...for citizens;"安全隐患排查整治"译 the investigation and rectification of potential safety hazards,搭配固定。 单复数"市民"指广大市民用复数 citizens;"城市"在"让城市更..."中泛指城市用复数 cities。

At the same time, it vigorously advances the systematic construction of urban infrastructure and conducts surveys of housing and municipal facilities as well as the investigation and rectification of potential safety hazards, striving to create a high-quality living environment for citizens and to make cities more beautiful, safer and more livable.
